CAS-093.q: Case – A group has a foreign subsidiary with USD functional currency. On consolidation in VND, translation differences are recognised:
CAS-093.e: Assets and liabilities at closing rates; income and expenses at transaction/average rates.
o: In OCI/equity (foreign currency translation reserve), reclassified to profit or loss on disposal
In profit or loss each year
CAS-093.x:
Basis: IAS 21 paras 39, 41, 48; VAS 10 paras 23–27 (translating foreign operations).
Analysis: Translating a USD-functional subsidiary into VND: assets and liabilities at the closing rate; income and expenses at transaction (or approximating average) rates; resulting differences go to OCI and accumulate in equity (translation reserve), reclassified to profit or loss on disposal.
Distractors: B and C – not annual profit or loss; D – not goodwill.

CAS-094.q: Case – A group is selling a business line (decided, buyer search under way, expected within 12 months). Under IFRS 5, it is:
CAS-094.e: IFRS 5 is the basis; VAS has no fully equivalent standard.
o: Classified as held for sale, measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell, depreciation stops; presented as discontinued if criteria are met
CAS-094.x:
Basis: IFRS 5 paras 6–8, 15, 25, 32–33.
Analysis: Held-for-sale criteria: available for immediate sale in present condition and highly probable (management committed, buyer search active, completion expected within 12 months). Then: measure at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell (CAS-095); stop depreciation; present separately; if a major separate line of business → present as discontinued operations.
Distractors: B – depreciation must stop; C – it hasn't been sold; D is insufficient.
Note: VAS has no full IFRS 5 equivalent.

CAS-095.q: Case – A group classifies a business line as held for sale under IFRS 5: carrying amount VND 500 billion; fair value 470 billion; costs to sell 10 billion. What impairment loss is recognised on classification (VND billion)?
CAS-095.e: Fair value less costs to sell = 460; loss = 500 − 460 = 40 billion VND.
CAS-095.x:
Basis: IFRS 5 paras 15, 20.
Working: Fair value less costs to sell = 470 − 10 = 460 billion; impairment = 500 − 460 = VND 40 billion.
Analysis: The loss first reduces the disposal group's goodwill, then pro rata the non-current assets within IFRS 5's measurement scope. A later fair value increase may be reversed up to the cumulative loss recognised.
Check: 460 + 40 = 500 ✓.

CAS-096.q: Case – Group internal audit builds a risk-based annual plan for 25 subsidiaries. Select ALL suitable prioritisation criteria:
CAS-096.e: Geographic proximity isn't a risk criterion.
o: Revenue/asset size and materiality to the group
Major changes: new leaders, new systems, M&A
Fraud and compliance risk by industry/country
CAS-096.x:
Basis: IIA GIAS 2024 (Principle 9 – strategic planning; standard 9.4 risk-based audit plan).
Analysis: Prioritisation criteria: (A) size and materiality to the group; (B) prior audit results and unresolved deficiencies; (C) major changes – new leaders, systems, M&A (ICA-014); (D) industry/country-specific fraud and compliance risks (FRD-092).
Distractors: (E) Proximity isn't a risk criterion – remote units are often riskier due to less oversight.

CAS-097.q: Case – A group is subject to the global minimum tax (Pillar Two); its Vietnamese subsidiary has a low effective rate due to incentives. The main consolidated FS effect under amended IAS 12:
CAS-097.e: Amended IAS 12 (2023) contains a mandatory temporary exception for Pillar Two deferred taxes.
o: Recognise current top-up tax, apply the temporary exception from deferred tax on Pillar Two and disclose exposure
Recognise full deferred tax for Pillar Two
CAS-097.x:
Basis: IAS 12 paras 4A, 88A–88D (May 2023 amendment – International Tax Reform, Pillar Two); Resolution 107/2023/QH15 on the global minimum tax.
Analysis: A Vietnamese subsidiary with a low effective rate (under 15%) from incentives → top-up tax may arise (Vietnam's qualified domestic minimum top-up tax or an IIR in the ultimate parent's country). Consolidated FS effects: recognise current top-up tax; apply the mandatory temporary exception – no recognition or disclosure of Pillar Two deferred taxes; disclose Pillar Two current tax separately and information on exposure.
Distractors: B – there is an effect; C contradicts the exception; D is wrong.
Note: Check current Vietnamese implementing guidance.

CAS-098.q: Case – When a group sells shares in a subsidiary but keeps control, the difference between proceeds and net assets transferred to NCI goes to equity (IFRS 10).
CAS-098.e: True. No gain/loss since control isn't lost.
CAS-098.x:
Basis: IFRS 10 para 23, B96.
Analysis: True. Ownership changes without losing control are transactions among owners → adjust the carrying amounts of the controlling interest and NCI; the difference between proceeds and the net assets attributed to NCI goes directly to the parent's equity, not profit or loss.
Note: Under Circular 202/2014/TT-BTC (VAS), this is likewise recorded in consolidated retained earnings, similar to IFRS.

CAS-099.q: Case – A group finds its subsidiary in a new market bribed officials to obtain licences. Beyond internal action, consolidated FS impacts to consider:
CAS-099.e: Non-compliance with laws can materially affect the FS (VSA 250).
o: Provisions/contingent liabilities for fines, licence revocation risk (asset impairment), reliability of subsidiary management representations, disclosure
CAS-099.x:
Basis: VSA 250 paras 18–22; IAS 37; IAS 36; VSA 580.
Analysis: Bribery to obtain permits at a subsidiary → consolidated effects: provisions or contingent liabilities for fines (local and extraterritorial law – ICA-081); licence revocation risk → impairment indicators (IAS 36), possibly the subsidiary's going concern; reliability of the subsidiary management's representations; disclosure.
Distractors: B and C ignore the effects; D – provisions/contingencies must be considered before any ruling.

CAS-100.q: Integrated case – A group preparing to list: profit +60%, negative operating cash flow, sharply rising related-party receivables, chief accountant changed twice, management awarded shares on successful listing. Select ALL reasonable auditor conclusions/responses:
CAS-100.e: Timetable pressure must not reduce audit quality; this is a classic red-flag combination (pressure + opportunity + financial signals).
o: Assess high fraudulent reporting risk, especially revenue and related-party transactions
Heighten scepticism, extend independent confirmations and substance testing
Test period-end entries, estimates and unusual transactions
Communicate red flags early with governance
Reduce audit scope to meet the listing timetable
CAS-100.x:
Basis: VSA 240 paras 26–30, appendix 1; VSA 550; VSA 260; VSA 220.
Analysis: A combination of red flags: pressure (listing, share bonuses on success), financial signals (profit +60% with negative CFO – FRD-036), opportunity/concealment (surging related-party receivables, two chief-accountant changes – AUD-074). Responses: (A) assess FS fraud risk as high, especially revenue and related parties; (B) heighten scepticism, extend independent confirmations, test substance; (C) test period-end journals, estimates and unusual transactions; (D) communicate early with governance.
Distractors: (E) Deadline pressure must not reduce audit quality (VSA 220).
